name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do a weekly automated scan of all prompts in our system, flagging duplicates and near-duplicates with high confidence. This cuts noise in routing and prevents wasted compute on redundant tasks. The trade-off is occasional false positives—we’ll miss some edge cases—but the time saved from cleaning up duplicates outweighs the risk.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is broken prompts hitting production before the weekly scan catches them—deployment-linked scans catch failures immediately, not after a week of accumulating duplicates. A better alternative is scanning at merge time: fail fast on duplicates, then auto-apply safe cleanups to reduce noise without the lag. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot comparing weekly vs. merge-time scans on the same set of prompts and measuring how many broken ones reach production in each case.
